episode_title: S1Ep301 Smarter Franchise Expansion with Kristie Kalinowski

real_qa.q: How does Hand and Stone distinguish between franchise opportunities that create strategic growth versus ones that just make the company bigger?
real_qa.r: Not every opportunity is the right opportunity for specific brands. When prospective franchise owners call with what they think is the best spot, Hand and Stone does the research to see if the unit can be supported. The best brands that continue to have smart and strategic growth are those that do not say yes to every opportunity, whether that be the franchise operator or the site. You need to look holistically for the betterment of your brand overall and say yes to the right opportunities.
real_qa.requete: Hand and Stone franchise opportunity selection strategy

real_qa.q: What can franchise development professionals identify in potential franchise owners within the first few minutes of conversation?
real_qa.r: Within about three minutes into a first conversation, you can tell if a franchise prospect is going to be something that has legs. It is about understanding someone's why—understanding why they want to be there and why they picked up the phone to inquire for that specific brand. If you can match their why to the company's long-term goals and see if those align, then you know that you have a path forward. If it is just about wanting to park money or throw money at something, generally that model does not work for brands focused on true entrepreneurship.
real_qa.requete: franchise owner vetting first conversation signs

real_qa.q: What key questions change the conversation when evaluating franchise deals and candidates at Hand and Stone?
real_qa.r: Understanding long-term vision is very important—where and how do potential owners see themselves doing this. At Hand and Stone, 70% of the system is multi-unit owned. Another critical question involves understanding their structure: are they willing and able to invest in a spa manager who will drive day-to-day operations, and do they want to be focused on the business overall while building the team beneath them to execute on a daily basis.
real_qa.requete: Hand and Stone multi-unit franchise owner questions

real_qa.q: What is Hand and Stone's membership model and how does it differ from traditional gym-style memberships?
real_qa.r: Hand and Stone's membership costs between $79.95 and $99.95 per month and provides one 50-minute service—either a massage or facial, with the choice being the customer's. Sessions roll over and members can gift between three and four sessions per year to other members or family members. It is not the traditional membership model where you feel locked in; members can use their membership nationwide, so traveling customers can use their sessions at any Hand and Stone location.
real_qa.requete: Hand and Stone membership rollover nationwide benefits

real_qa.q: What are Hand and Stone's 2025 performance metrics and current market expansion priorities?
real_qa.r: Hand and Stone delivered 1.6 million facials in 2025, making them the number one provider of facials in the world on an aggregate basis. The company now has 650 locations plus across the U.S. and Canada, reaching toward the 700 mark and serving over 600,000 members. Hand and Stone is currently underdeveloped in Boston, Southern California, and Northern California, with market incentives for those that qualify for multi-unit development of a 10-pack.
real_qa.requete: Hand and Stone 1.6 million facials 2025 locations expansion
